summary: This program takes a list of Song objects and feeds them into a PriorityQueue whose comparator ranks songs by energy level from highest to lowest, then drains the queue with poll() so the songs come out in that order.

lines.text: Comparator is the interface that lets you describe a custom ordering rule; the PriorityQueue below needs one because Song has no built-in notion of "comes first."
A PriorityQueue keeps its elements ordered by priority rather than by insertion order, so whatever you remove next is always the highest-priority item.

lines.code: // Example: Playlist as a PriorityQueue of Song objects by energy (High → Low)
lines.text: The earlier comments stand in for the parts of the chapter's playlist app you already built; this is the section the exercise asks you to write.
The queue now holds whole Song objects instead of plain strings, which is why it needs to be told how to compare them.
comparingInt builds a comparator that reads each song's energyLevel, and reversed() flips it so the largest number is treated as the highest priority.
addAll copies every song from the existing playlist into the queue, and each insertion is slotted into place according to the comparator.
Draining a queue is a loop that keeps going until nothing is left, since each poll() shrinks the queue by one.

lines.code: Song nextSong = energyQueue.poll(); // highest energy first
lines.text: poll() removes and returns the front of the queue, which under this comparator is always the remaining song with the greatest energy level.
Concatenating a Song onto a string calls its toString method, so the Song class controls how each track appears here.
